checks.item: start_year -331: Alexandria founded by Alexander the Great
checks.found: Wikipedia: 'Alexandria was founded by Alexander the Great in April 331 BC'; infobox established 331 BC. EB1911: 'Founded in 332 B.C. by Alexander the Great'.
checks.detail: Year and event match the cited page; the 332 alternative is disclosed in the source string and notes.

checks.found: Row 'Alexandria, Egypt': AD_1 = 400000. EB1911: 'In the Augustan age the population of Alexandria was estimated at 300,000 free folk, in addition to an immense number of slaves.'
checks.detail: Exact match; the note's Britannica figure also checks out.

checks.found: Text: 'In 1897, the city had 315,844 inhabitants'. Appendix 1, 'Population of Alexandria by qism between 1897 - 1947': Total Alexandria 1897 = 315,844 (source: CAPMAS population censuses).
checks.detail: Number, year and area (city total of qisms) match.

checks.item: Pharos (Lighthouse of Alexandria): completed -280, height 103 m, at 31.2148, 29.886 (estimated)
checks.found: Infobox height 103 to 118 m (McKenzie 2011, p. 42); 'Arab descriptions ... Given heights vary only fifteen percent from 103 to 118 m'; built 'during the reign of Ptolemy II Philadelphus (280-247 BC)'; deactivated 1303; last stones reused in 1480 for the Citadel of Qaitbay; coord 31.2148, 29.886.
checks.detail: Height range, position, the 1303 ruin and the approximate date match; the point is already marked estimated with a note that the year is approximate and the height is the low end of the range.

checks.item: Pompey's Pillar: completed 298, height 26.85 m, at 31.1825, 29.8964 (documented)
checks.found: 'set up in honour of the Roman emperor Diocletian between 298-302 AD'; infobox 'built AD 298-303 (dedicated)', height '26.85 m (present total)', about 33.85 m with the 7 m statue; 'stands some 26.85 m high, including its base and capital' (Delbrück 2007, pp. 100-101); coord 31°10'57"N 29°53'47.1"E (31.1825, 29.8964).
checks.detail: Height and position confirmed. The year is flagged: the page gives only a range (298 to 302, or 303 in the infobox), so 298 is the earliest possible date, not a completion date, and the page does not settle a single year. Added a sentence to the point's note in alexandria.json; value and confidence left unchanged.

checks.item: Citadel of Qaitbay: completed 1477, height 17 m, at 31.213, 29.8852 (estimated)
checks.found: Infobox: built 1477, height 17 m (cited to a blog); text: 'built from 1477 to 1479 AD'; coord 31.2130, 29.8852.
checks.detail: Height and position match and 1477 is the page's stated build year (construction ran to 1479); already marked estimated, which suits the weak height citation.

checks.item: -47: Caesar's siege of Alexandria (Library damaged; Octavian later placed the city under a Roman prefect)
checks.found: Wikipedia: 'Library of Alexandria, which faced destruction during Caesar's siege of Alexandria in 47 BC'. EB1911: 'Julius Caesar dallied with Cleopatra in 47 B.C. and was mobbed by the rabble ... Octavian, who placed over it a prefect from the imperial household'.
checks.detail: Year and each element of the description are supported by the two cited pages.

checks.item: 2002: Bibliotheca Alexandrina inaugurated (seafront near the harbour, design by Snøhetta, opened October 2002)
checks.found: 'The complex was officially inaugurated in 2002'; 'built during the 1990s on the Mediterranean Sea coastline near the harbor of Alexandria ... opened in October 2002'; the 1988 UNESCO design competition 'was won by Snøhetta'.
checks.detail: Year, month, location and architect match.

summary: Nine of 10 sampled figures match their sources, including the three Modelski estimates and the 1897 census total. One flag: Pompey's Pillar is dated by its source only to 298-302/303, so the stored year 298 is the start of a range rather than a completion date; a note was added and nothing else changed.
